concepts.title: Area of Jurisdiction of a Police Station

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Area of Jurisdiction of a Police Station' refers to.
questions.a: The defined geographic territory assigned to a specific police post, within which officers are authorised to register and investigate complaints.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Area of Jurisdiction of a Police Station'.
questions.a: Every police station has a designated geographic boundary for reporting and investigating local cases.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Area of Jurisdiction of a Police Station' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Area of the Police Station (source: fess306.txt lines 50-70)

concepts.title: Role and Work at the Police Station

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role and Work at the Police Station' refers to.
questions.a: The official duties of police personnel and the Station House Officer, including logging written complaints, investigating offenses, and preserving peace.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role and Work at the Police Station'.
questions.a: The Station House Officer records written complaints and dispatches officers to investigate reported incidents.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role and Work at the Police Station' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: The work at the Police Station (source: fess306.txt lines 70-100)

concepts.title: Role and Duties of the Patwari

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Role and Duties of the Patwari' refers to.
questions.a: A local administrative official tasked with measuring land plots, maintaining ownership registers, and updating village maps.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Role and Duties of the Patwari'.
questions.a: The Patwari measures land plots, keeps records updated, and assists in land revenue collection for a cluster of villages.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Role and Duties of the Patwari' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maintenance of Land Records (source: fess306.txt lines 100-130)

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Khasra Records and Land Maps' refers to.
questions.a: A official village register kept by land officials detailing individual plot numbers, owners, area sizes, crop types, and irrigation sources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Khasra Records and Land Maps'.
questions.a: Khasra records provide accurate tabular details that correspond directly to village land maps.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Khasra Records and Land Maps' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maintenance of Land Records (source: fess306.txt lines 130-160)

concepts.title: Structure and Role of the Revenue Department

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Structure and Role of the Revenue Department' refers to.
questions.a: The government administrative hierarchy headed by the District Collector and Tehsildars that oversees land record management and resolves property disputes.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Structure and Role of the Revenue Department'.
questions.a: Tehsildars supervise Patwaris, resolve land disputes, collect revenue, and issue essential government certificates.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Structure and Role of the Revenue Department' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maintenance of Land Records (source: fess306.txt lines 160-190)

concepts.title: Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005

questions.q: Calculate the equal land share allocated to each family member. Use the method 'Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005'. Work with: total_heirs = 240, total_land = 100. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share.
questions.a: 0.4167 as a fraction

questions.q: Find the area of inherited land received per heir. Use the method 'Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005'. Work with: total_heirs = 40, total_land = 2500. Carry the chain through step by step and give the final value of share.
questions.a: 62.5 units

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005' refers to.
questions.a: The mathematical division of inherited ancestral land equally among all eligible legal heirs, including sons, daughters, and mother, under legal reform guidelines.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005'.
questions.a: The total agricultural land is divided equally among all eligible heirs.

questions.q: Write the standard relation used for 'Equal Land Share Calculation under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005', in plain ASCII form.
questions.a: share = total_land / total_heirs

concepts.title: Equal Rights under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Equal Rights under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005' refers to.
questions.a: A legal reform that ensures sons, daughters, and mothers possess identical ownership rights in ancestral family agricultural land.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Equal Rights under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005'.
questions.a: The 2005 amendment removed gender discrimination in the inheritance of family agricultural land.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Equal Rights under Hindu Succession Amendment Act, 2005' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: A New Law (source: fess306.txt lines 190-220)

concepts.title: Public Services and Local Amenities in Rural Areas

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Public Services and Local Amenities in Rural Areas' refers to.
questions.a: Government facilities and local civic administration networks, such as fair price shops, healthcare centers, and milk cooperatives, serving rural citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Public Services and Local Amenities in Rural Areas'.
questions.a: Government departments manage essential public facilities that require civic monitoring and continuous improvement.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Public Services and Local Amenities in Rural Areas' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Other Public Services - A survey (source: fess306.txt lines 220-260)
